startUrl.title: ClinicalTrials.gov search URL
startUrl.description: Optional shortcut: build the search on clinicaltrials.gov, then paste the address bar here — e.g. "https://clinicaltrials.gov/search?cond=asthma&aggFilters=status:rec,phase:3". An API URL ("https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.cond=asthma") works too. The URL's search terms (condition, other terms, intervention, sponsor, location, title, outcome, lead sponsor, study IDs) REPLACE the matching fields below, and its status/phase/study-type/funder/sex/age/results/documents filters are applied as-is. Everything the URL does not mention (max results, row mode, watch label, and any filter below it doesn't carry) still applies.

nctIds.title: Specific NCT IDs (direct lookup)
nctIds.description: One or more ClinicalTrials.gov study IDs (e.g. "NCT04368728, NCT03854955" — comma, space or newline separated). When set, this is an EXCLUSIVE lookup mode: every other filter below (conditions, status, phase, etc.) is ignored, so a mixed batch of trials on unrelated topics still all come back. Malformed or nonexistent ids are dropped individually with a named warning instead of failing the whole run.

conditions.title: Conditions / diseases
conditions.description: Condition or disease terms, e.g. "breast cancer". Maps to query.cond. Leave empty with a search query or overallStatus filter, or every study since 1999 matches.

interventions.title: Interventions / treatments
interventions.description: Drug, device or procedure name, e.g. "pembrolizumab". Maps to query.intr.

sponsors.title: Sponsor / collaborator name
sponsors.description: Lead sponsor or collaborator organization name. Maps to query.spons.

locations.title: Location (city, state or country)
locations.description: Facility location text, e.g. "Boston, Massachusetts". Maps to query.locn.

searchQuery.title: Free-text search
searchQuery.description: General search term across titles, outcomes and eligibility text. Maps to query.term.

overallStatus.title: Recruitment status
overallStatus.description: Filter by recruitment status. Leave empty for all statuses.

studyTypes.title: Study type
studyTypes.description: Interventional, observational or expanded-access. Leave empty for all.

phases.title: Phase
phases.description: Trial phase. Only meaningful for interventional studies; ~19% of all studies have no phase at all (observational studies, device trials). Leave empty for all.

resultsAvailability.title: Posted results
resultsAvailability.description: Filter on whether the study has posted a results section on ClinicalTrials.gov. "With results" is the endpoint set for outcome/efficacy analysis; "without results" finds completed trials that never reported (an FDAAA-compliance use case).

hasResultsOnly.title: Only studies with posted results (legacy)
hasResultsOnly.description: Deprecated — use "Posted results" above instead. Kept so older saved inputs keep working; equivalent to setting "Posted results" to "with". Ignored if "Posted results" is set.

ageGroups.title: Age group
ageGroups.description: Restrict to studies enrolling these standard age groups (child = birth–17, adult = 18–64, older adult = 65+). A study can belong to several. Leave empty for all.

documentTypes.title: Has study document
documentTypes.description: Only studies that have uploaded one of these documents to ClinicalTrials.gov (multiple selections are OR-ed). Roughly 9% of studies have any — useful when you need the actual protocol or analysis plan, not just the registry summary.

fdaRegulationViolation.title: Only studies with an FDAAA violation notice
fdaRegulationViolation.description: Restrict to the small set of studies flagged with an FDA regulation (FDAAA 801) violation notice — currently a few dozen registry-wide. Leave off for normal searches.

sex.title: Eligible sex
sex.description: Restrict to studies whose eligibility criteria specify this sex. Leave blank for all (most studies are open to all).

acceptsHealthyVolunteers.title: Accepts healthy volunteers
acceptsHealthyVolunteers.description: Restrict to studies that accept healthy volunteers (not just patients with the condition).

lastUpdatePostedDateFrom.title: Last updated from
lastUpdatePostedDateFrom.description: Only studies whose ClinicalTrials.gov record was last updated on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Useful for a repeatable "what changed since I last pulled" run.

lastUpdatePostedDateTo.title: Last updated to
lastUpdatePostedDateTo.description: Only studies whose ClinicalTrials.gov record was last updated on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

ageRangeFromYears.title: Minimum eligibility age from (years)
ageRangeFromYears.description: Only studies whose stated minimum eligibility age is at least this many years (e.g. 18 to exclude studies open to minors). Leave blank for no lower bound.

ageRangeToYears.title: Maximum eligibility age to (years)
ageRangeToYears.description: Only studies whose stated maximum eligibility age is at most this many years (e.g. 65 to exclude studies with no senior-age cap). Leave blank for no upper bound.

funderTypes.title: Funder / lead sponsor type
funderTypes.description: Restrict to studies whose lead sponsor is this type of organization. Leave empty for all.

titleOrAcronym.title: Title or acronym contains
titleOrAcronym.description: Search only the study's official/brief title and acronym (not eligibility text or outcomes). Maps to query.titles. Narrower than the general free-text search above.

outcomeMeasure.title: Outcome measure contains
outcomeMeasure.description: Search only the study's stated outcome measures, e.g. "progression-free survival" or "overall survival". Maps to query.outc.

studyStartDateFrom.title: Study start from
studyStartDateFrom.description: Only studies whose start date is on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Maps to AREA[StartDate].

studyStartDateTo.title: Study start to
studyStartDateTo.description: Only studies whose start date is on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Maps to AREA[StartDate].

primaryCompletionDateFrom.title: Primary completion from
primaryCompletionDateFrom.description: Only studies whose primary completion date is on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Maps to AREA[PrimaryCompletionDate].

primaryCompletionDateTo.title: Primary completion to
primaryCompletionDateTo.description: Only studies whose primary completion date is on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Maps to AREA[PrimaryCompletionDate].

studyCompletionDateFrom.title: Study completion from
studyCompletionDateFrom.description: Only studies whose overall completion date is on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Maps to AREA[CompletionDate].

studyCompletionDateTo.title: Study completion to
studyCompletionDateTo.description: Only studies whose overall completion date is on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Maps to AREA[CompletionDate].

firstPostedDateFrom.title: First posted from
firstPostedDateFrom.description: Only studies first posted to ClinicalTrials.gov on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Use this to find newly registered trials. Maps to AREA[StudyFirstPostDate].

firstPostedDateTo.title: First posted to
firstPostedDateTo.description: Only studies first posted to ClinicalTrials.gov on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Maps to AREA[StudyFirstPostDate].

resultsFirstPostedDateFrom.title: Results first posted from
resultsFirstPostedDateFrom.description: Only studies whose results were first posted on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Maps to AREA[ResultsFirstPostDate].

resultsFirstPostedDateTo.title: Results first posted to
resultsFirstPostedDateTo.description: Only studies whose results were first posted on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Maps to AREA[ResultsFirstPostDate].

facilityName.title: Facility name
facilityName.description: Only studies running at a facility whose name matches this text, e.g. "Mayo Clinic". This is the site/hospital name, not the city — use "Location" above for a city/state/country. Maps to AREA[LocationFacility].

leadSponsorName.title: Lead sponsor name (exact field)
leadSponsorName.description: Only studies whose LEAD sponsor name matches this text, e.g. "Pfizer". Unlike "Sponsor / collaborator name" above (which also matches collaborators and other free-text sponsor fields), this restricts to the lead sponsor only. Maps to AREA[LeadSponsorName].

sortBy.title: Sort order
sortBy.description: How ClinicalTrials.gov orders results (before maxResults truncates them). Default is the API's own relevance order.

rowsPerStudy.title: Row mode
rowsPerStudy.description: "study" = one row per trial (default). "site" = one row per trial site/facility — what site-selection and patient-recruitment buyers need. A single study averages 5 sites (max seen: 110), so site mode returns roughly 5x more billable rows for the same query.

maxResults.title: Max results
maxResults.description: Stop after this many rows (studies, or sites if rowsPerStudy="site"). Token-based paging has no offset wall.

watchLabel.title: Watch label (only new since last run)
watchLabel.description: Optional. Name a saved search (e.g. "my-oncology-watch") and this run returns ONLY studies not delivered under that same label and filter set before, instead of the full match set every time. The first run for a label is a free baseline: it records what already matches and returns zero rows. Run it again later -- on a schedule, typically -- to get only what's new. The baseline is kept in your own Apify account (a named key-value store), keyed by label plus a fingerprint of your other filters, so changing a filter starts a fresh baseline instead of dumping previously-excluded studies as "new". Ignored when nctIds is set.

watchChanges.title: Also alert on study changes
watchChanges.description: Only used with watchLabel. When on, a study you were already alerted on is re-delivered (charged again) if ClinicalTrials.gov's own Last Update Posted date moves, or its overall status, enrollment count, primary completion date or completion date changes (e.g. Recruiting -> Completed, a protocol amendment, a readout date slipping) -- tagged with _watchChangeType and _watchPrevious showing exactly what moved. Off by default, so a plain watchLabel only ever alerts on brand-new studies, same as before this option existed.
